# Sirach Chapter 34 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_034_page_001.jpg

---

34:1 Foolish people put their hope in empty illusions, and dreams give fools something to get excited about.

34:2 Paying attention to dreams is like grasping at shadows or trying to catch the wind.

34:3 A dream is nothing more than a reflection — like seeing your own face mirrored back to you.

34:4 How can something unclean produce anything clean? How can something false tell you anything true?

34:5 Divination, omens, and dreams are all empty. When your mind fantasizes during sleep, it's no different from the irrational panic of a woman in labor.

34:6 The only exception is when the Most High sends a dream as a message. If that's not the case, don't give it a second thought.

34:7 Dreams have led many people badly astray, and everyone who has put their trust in them has been disappointed.

34:8 God's instruction needs no lie to be fulfilled. True wisdom is found in the mouths of people who can be trusted.

34:9 A person who has traveled widely has picked up a great deal of knowledge; someone with real-world experience can speak with genuine understanding.

34:10 Someone who has never been anywhere knows very little; but the well-traveled person has developed real insight.

34:11 In my own travels I've seen a great deal, and I understand more than I'm able to put into words.

34:12 I've been in situations where I nearly lost my life more than once — and those very dangers taught me things.

34:13 The life of those who fear the Lord will be sustained, because they place their hope in the God who rescues them.

34:14 Those who fear the Lord have nothing to be afraid of — they won't crumble under pressure, because the Lord is their hope.

34:15 How blessed is the person who fears the Lord! Who else do they need? Who else can support them like God?

34:16 The Lord's eyes are on those who love him — he is their powerful shield and strong support, shelter from scorching wind, shade from the noonday sun, protection from stumbling, and rescue from falling.

34:17 He revives the spirit, makes the eyes shine with new life, and gives healing, vitality, and blessing.

34:18 Bringing an offering from stolen goods — the offering is tainted, and God finds no pleasure in gifts from lawbreakers.

34:19 The Most High doesn't enjoy the offerings of ungodly people. Piling up sacrifices won't make him forgive sins.

34:20 Offering a sacrifice made from what you've stolen from the poor is like killing a son in front of his father's eyes.

34:21 For poor people, their daily bread is their very life. To take it from them is to take their lives.

34:22 Cheating someone out of their livelihood is murder. Withholding wages from a worker is as good as shedding their blood.

34:23 What do you get when one person builds and another tears it down? Nothing but wasted effort.

34:24 If one person prays while another is cursing you, whose prayer do you think God will answer?

34:25 If you wash off ritual impurity and then immediately go back and touch the corpse again, what did the washing accomplish?

34:26 It's the same with someone who fasts as penance for sins and then immediately goes back to doing the same things. Who will hear that prayer? What good did the fasting do?
